name: Brand Book
title: Brand Book: operator paths, consumers and what can go wrong

BANDS.s: Opening the Brand Book for a location and what is there on first visit
Logos, colours, fonts with their Done mark, content images, brand voice and social links
The Save button, what is sent and what the server stores
Website builder sync, new website drafts, emails, menu boards and media pickers
Editing or deleting brand items after other products already use them

NODES.d: The operator opens Marketing, Brand Book in Web Dash. Access is behind the Brand Book feature permission. The Brand Book belongs to the selected restaurant (location).
e: Multi-location brand must set up the same Brand Book once per location, with no copy between locations
Duplicate work and drift between stores
Permission missing, the page is simply absent from the sidebar

NODES.d: On first visit the page shows default items: Heading, Sub-heading and Paragraph fonts, default colours and a list of brand voice options. No AI generated Brand Book from the restaurant details or an existing website was found in the live code.
e: Defaults look like a finished brand, operator never customises them and every consumer uses generic styles
Page loads with a spinner and no data when the content request fails, with no error message
Restaurant logo already uploaded elsewhere (online ordering, receipts) is not offered here

NODES.d: The operator uploads one or more logos through a signed upload to file storage; each is saved as a logo item linked to the stored file.
e: Logo variants (light, dark, icon) are not labelled, consumers pick the first one even when it does not suit a dark background
Invisible logo on dark headers or boards
Very large or transparent-less logo files accepted without guidance
Upload succeeds but the save never happens, the file sits in storage unlinked

NODES.d: The operator adds, names and edits colours stored as hex values.
e: No contrast check between brand colours, text and background combinations built from them are unreadable
Colour names are free text with no role (primary, accent, background), consumers cannot tell which colour to use where
Invalid or short hex value accepted

NODES.d: Heading, Sub-heading and Paragraph fonts each have family, style, size, weight, line height and letter spacing, from the font list or an uploaded custom font. Each font item is edited open and must be marked Done; Save skips any font still open and is disabled while a default font is open.
e: Sub-heading and Paragraph fonts not marked Done are never saved, so they are missing for every consumer
Website sync crashes or does nothing
Done mark is easy to miss and there is no unsaved state per font
Empty font family silently saved as Poppins
Custom uploaded font not available on the published website
Fonts fall back on the live site

NODES.d: The operator adds brand photos to the content library (compressed on upload), used later as media in other products.
e: Image deleted here while used by a website, email or board
No rights or source recorded for uploaded photos

NODES.d: The operator selects brand voice options (tone words) and can add custom ones. The campaign SMS writing assistant includes the active voice selections in its generation request.
e: An outdated voice is still selected when a campaign is rewritten
The generated text sounds wrong for the restaurant
Removing a custom voice and saving deletes it with no undo

NODES.d: Links for social networks (Facebook, Instagram, X, TikTok and so on) that feed the website footer icons.
e: Link saved without https or as a handle, website icon goes nowhere
Network name not mapped to a website icon, the link is ignored on sync

NODES.d: One Save button sends every colour, voice, closed font, social link and logo plus a list of deleted items. There is a leave page warning for unsaved changes.
e: Save fails and only logs to the console, the button returns to Save with no error
Two managers save at once, the later save overwrites the other's changes
Fonts left open are silently left out of the save

NODES.d: The server creates new items, updates changed ones by id and deletes the ids listed as removed, and the Brand Book updated date moves on so the website builder can spot the change.
e: An edit or deletion affects an item owned by another restaurant
Creates, updates and deletes are not in one transaction, a failure leaves a half saved brand
Updated date not moved when only a delete happens, the website never offers a sync

NODES.d: On success the page reloads the saved items and refreshes the cached Brand Book for other screens.
e: Other open screens keep a cached Brand Book until reloaded
Consumers show old colours or logos

NODES.d: When the website builder opens, it compares the Brand Book updated date with the copy stored in the draft and, if newer, shows New changes made in brand book with Later or Sync now.
e: Change only noticed when someone opens the builder, the live website keeps the old brand indefinitely
Each draft tracks its own copy, syncing one draft leaves the others out of date

NODES.d: Sync now copies fonts (only properties that changed), logos, colours and social links into the draft and shows a success message. Colours go to the palette but do not rewrite section colour styles. The live site changes only after republishing.
e: Sync now crashes or fails to bring the saved Brand Book changes into the site
Sync overwrites font changes made by hand in the builder for the same property
Changed colours do not update colour styles in use, so the site does not look different after sync
Success shown even when the Brand Book request failed

NODES.t: New website draft takes the brand
NODES.d: When a new website draft is created, the builder applies all Brand Book fonts to the global text and button styles, sets social links and stores a copy of the Brand Book.
e: Missing fonts leave template defaults in place without a warning
Site does not match the brand
Empty Brand Book gives a generic site

NODES.t: Use brand assets in campaign content
NODES.d: The campaign and journey email builders offer Brand Book colours in the colour palette and Brand Book images and logos in media pickers. Values are copied into each email when chosen. The SMS rewrite request also includes active brand voices.
e: Brand colour changed later, emails already built keep the old colour
Logo deleted from the Brand Book, scheduled emails show a broken image

NODES.d: The menu board canvas offers Brand Book colours, fonts and logos and keeps a reference to the Brand Book colour on elements that use it.
e: Brand colour deleted while a board element still references it
Board falls back to a default colour
Brand font not available on the TV app
Font falls back on the board

NODES.d: Deals, spotlights, gift cards and other forms offer Brand Book content images in their image pickers.
e: Image removed from the Brand Book disappears from live deals or gift card designs
Large uncompressed images chosen for small slots

NODES.d: The operator changes fonts, colours, logos or links after other products already use them, then saves again.
e: Operator expects every product to update automatically, but website, emails and boards only change when each is re-synced, edited or republished
Re-opening a font to edit it removes it from the next save until marked Done again

NODES.d: Colours, voices, social links and logos removed on the page are deleted on the next save.
e: No check whether the item is used by a website, email or board before deleting
Deleting all fonts or colours leaves consumers with nothing to read

NODES.d: The brand is stored and the consumers that were synced or edited show it.
e: No single view of which products are using an out of date Brand Book

NOTES: No AI generation of the Brand Book (from restaurant details or an existing website) was found in the live code; first-time set-up is manual with default items.
The campaign copy request reads active brand voices for SMS suggestions. Check the saved selection when the generated tone is unexpected.
The Save button is now disabled while a default font is still open, a guard added after the Done related tickets; non-default fonts left open are still skipped.
Engineering should confirm that every Brand Book change is limited to assets owned by the selected restaurant.
Menu boards, email builders and media pickers were confirmed to read the Brand Book from file names and imports; exact live versus copy behaviour per consumer was assumed to be copy on choose.
The Brand Book is per restaurant (location); no copy between locations was found.
